methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $65M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Vulcan Elements is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by John Maslin and Piotr Kulik that has raised $65M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 9 comparable companies: 1 public entity and 8 private firms spanning the robotics and manufacturing sector, including Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Walden Robotics.

Two triangulation methods apply to this valuation. Stage-progression analysis, using total raised as a proxy and applying a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A to next-stage transitions, implies a valuation of $130M. Peer-median analysis draws on four same-sector and same/adjacent-stage comparables with a median valuation of $1.7B and a range of $1.1B to $2.0B, directly implying $1.7B for Vulcan Elements.

These methods produce a wide triangulated range of $110M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $915M. The stage-progression method is most conservative, reflecting limited visibility into company-specific traction. The peer-median method anchors toward growth-stage valuations, as three of four peers have progressed to Series B. Key uncertainties include Vulcan's relative technical differentiation within the peer set, revenue traction relative to comparables, and whether Series B momentum in robotics will sustain. A point estimate within $400M–$1.4B would be defensible pending diligence into unit economics and market timing.
